lab_ambient_temperature.text:
{
  "entry_id": "lab_ambient_temperature",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. Because nothing actuates the sample temperature on this instrument, this is an ambient value of the room rather than a setpoint -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.",
  "numbers": [
    { "name": "ambient_temperature", "value": 293, "unit": "K", "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917", "grade": "E3", "precision": "significant_figures", "note": "the reading was reported as 20 degrees Celsius. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading." }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. Two things are still open and neither may be assumed. WHERE the thermometer is -- room air or close to the sample -- is not recorded, so this is the laboratory's ambient temperature and it is not established to be the sample's; a plan that needs the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. And the drift band is unmeasured: with no actuator, that band is not a tolerance anyone chooses but a property of the room somebody has to measure. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot. The date the reading was taken is not recorded either -- what is dated 2026-09-17 is the operator's statement that it is a reading.",
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_20260917",
  "date": "2026-09-17",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

tau_d.text:
{
  "entry_id": "tau_d",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "derived_quantity",
  "claim": "The diffusive time is the time a sphere needs to diffuse its own diameter, and it sets the shortest record length from which a mean squared displacement can be read.",
  "symbol": "tau_d",
  "formula": "bead_diameter**2/diffusivity",
  "inputs": ["bead_diameter", "diffusivity"],
  "unit": "s",
  "validity_conditions": "A length squared over a diffusivity is a TIME, and the unit above says so: this is a derived quantity that keeps a dimension, not a dimensionless group. Physically: spherical tracer, bulk fluid, no slip, overdamped. Near a wall the drag is corrected separately rather than absorbed into this time, or the time unit changes with stage position and nothing can be compared.",
